newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japan firms aim to merge in telecoms reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Two Japan firms aim to merge in telecoms reshuffle.

text.p: Two Japanese telecoms companies said on Wednesday they were aiming to work out a merger pact by the end of the month, a move analysts said signalled the start of a long-anticipated industry shakeup.

Japan Telecom Co Ltd, Japan's third-biggest long-distance carrier, said if an agreement was reached by the end of March, overseas carrier International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ) would be merged with his firm around October.

"It would be difficult to survive if we operate only long-distance services," Japan Telecom's vice president Haruo Murakami said in a news conference, citing a growing trend for one-stop shopping services on the global market.
One-stop shopping allows consumers to access seamless global communications services ranging from city to international calls through single supplier.

Murakami said the merger would also give Japan Telecom an edge in talks with international telecoms consortia as it hopes to join one of the three global groupings -- WorldPartners, Concert and Global One.
The telecom titan and the two firms' biggest rival, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, said the moves went with the "industry stream".

"I have said that the restructuring of NTT, and its entry into international services, would spark an industry realignment," NTT president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference. "Many other tie-ups and mergers will follow."
But asked about NTT's own international strategy, Miyazu reiterated his stance that NTT will not tie up with just one particular international consortium.
"We will probably tie up with various firms, depending on services and regions," he said.

The merger between Japan Telecom and ITJ will create a company with annual sales of some 400 billion yen ($3.25 billion) -- still no match for NTT, which has sales of six trillion yen ($48.7 billion) a year.

Japan Telecom told a news conference it had hopes for further tie-ups in the future, including one with Japan's top international carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD), which has close links with nine telecom affiliates of electric power utilities.
KDD is already allied with WorldPartners, a loosely knit group led by U.S. telecoms giant AT & T Corp.
Concert links British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp of the United States, while Global One groups Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp.

Analysts said the restructuring signalled by the proposed merger was inevitable given Japan's moves to deregulate the sector, harsh global competition and the domestic dominance of NTT, now poised to enter the international telecoms field.
"It's the first sign of a significant reorganisation in the international market, which was inevitable," said Andrew Haskins, an analyst at HSBC James Capel Japan.

"The situation in the international market is that there are three (Japanese) operators, none of which is large enough on a global scale and which are facing a massive increase in competition from foreign operators and from domestic operators like NTT," Haskins said.
ITJ is one of Japan's smaller overseas carriers. The other two are former monopoly KDD and unlisted IDC Corp.

Under a plan worked out late last year, NTT is set to be restructured into a set of firms including one which will operate international services, under the wing of a holding company. Japan's legal barriers between international and domestic telecoms business will be dismantled from April.
The biggest issue now is when DDI Corp -- currently Japan's second-largest phone operator -- will join in a new domestic grouping.
Industry circles are also watching IDC, the last international carrier, which has a close relationship with NTT. ($1=123 yen)
